body.p: A bear came to the hares. The hares climbed up middle pole [of the tent] and said: "The bear starts to shamanize", they put rotten wood into the blanket. The bear caught the tent pole and started to shamanize, he said: "Lungs of the hares, chanes, chanes!" The hares said: "What is the old one doing? Open your eyes." Then they poured the stuff into his eyes, which they had stuck into their stockings. The bear became blind. The hares said: What is the old one doing?" The bird cherries are ripe. Old one, the [DCh]: Form "inÅiktÉkÉËrÉ" is not clear; really ACC.INDF?; [VGM:] The bear's eyes are called "bird cherries" in taboo language.[DCh]: Not ears are furry." (?) The old one named Kandika came to the hares and asked: "Where did the bear go?"found in dictionaries, 'ear' is "seËn". "lapu" looks like russ. "lapa" 'paw'. "He went there!" There she found him, caught him and told the hares: "Bring a table." There she made the bear slip. The old one returned home. Old one, we are starting to get bored, we are going to leave!" The hares left and the old one said: "Leave along the [path that is like a] hoof, not the [one like a] sleeping bag." They went along the [path that is like a] sleeping bag. At the crossroads, the first one said: "Where should we go?" One of them said: "[The path that is] hoof-like." "Wait, let us fight!"[DCh]: The verb They started to fight. "Whoever wins leaves along the [path like a] sleeping bag." The younger sibling won forms are strange; no tense/mood marker.[DCh]: Not clear why interrogative "ir" 'where'.and the two of them went along the [path like a] sleeping bag. They walked and walked and were surrounded there. The hare said: "Having become a pine needle, I leave." The other said: "Having become a pine cone." The one being a pine needle went out. The pine cone left as well. The younger one carried it, put it on a stump and started to cry. He put it on a rock, started to cry again, put it on a log, started to cry again. Again, he put it on a rock and then left. He went to the frogs. He started to live with the frogs. He told a frog: "Let us visit relatives." The hare took an iron needle case, the frog boasted: "Good needle case!" The frog said: "My steel [DCh]: Why "ÐºÑÐ°ÑÐ¸Ð²ÑÐ¹" in Russian translation instead of "Ð¸Ð³Ð¾Ð»ÑÐ½Ð¸Ðº"?needle case, do ring the bell!" It rang the bell, he said to the frog: "Let us visit relatives." The hare left. He arrived and his older sister, that he left, had married a god. There, in the hole of a log, reindeer rang bells. The older sister said: "Ring." It rang beyond the clouds. The reindeer came. The reindeer were very big. The hare brought his older sister's reindeer home. He came home. The frog brought insects. The reindeer brought insects with their hooves. While running home the hare said to the frog: "Wind is coming." The wind carried the frog's house away. The frog dove into the lake.
